question: 7:168/q17
position: Inwardly, good deeds involve witnessing the divine agent and forgetting oneself; sins involve wavering and conspicuous awareness of oneself.
reasons: Al-Qushayrī says good deeds are acts in which the divine agent is witnessed without distraction from the Originator, while sins involve wavering between action and delay, permission and shortcoming. A saying he reports adds that a good deed makes one forget oneself, while a sin makes the self conspicuous.

question: 7:168/q17
position: Inwardly, good deeds are wakeful moments and days free of affliction; sins are divine abandonment and continuing deprivation.
reasons: Al-Qushayrī reports this as another saying about good deeds and sins.

question: 7:168/q23
position: God lets people proceed according to His knowledge of whether they will become righteous or corrupt.
reasons: Al-Qushayrī says God gives people scope to proceed in keeping with what He knows they will become: sound and righteous or corrupt and disobedient.

question: What follows when divine warning and respite fail to bring people back?

positions.position: God warns people to establish the case, then punishes them if admonition fails; once respite ends and a servant is rejected, there is no recovery.
positions.reasons: Al-Qushayrī says God gives warning and advance instruction before destroying those unmoved by admonition. He says the end of respite leaves only annihilation and a servant fallen from God's regard never recovers. He likens rejection to dismissal by a king and cites an anonymous poem about lasting rejection.
